title: P4-15: Pretext width cache is not cleared after web fonts load, so some loads wrap with fallback widths
description: Found by the Threat Intelligence scaffold (P4-04, Threat-Intelligence#10): with Google-loaded fonts (brand fonts slot, Papyrus#150) the Pretext text measurement races the font load. Papyrus never clears Pretext width cache once the fonts are ready, so some page loads wrap lines with fallback-font widths and clip lines (edition height 17328 px vs 17648 px baseline when fonts load in time). Fix in Papyrus (lib/pretext-layout.ts, hooks use-brand-fonts-ready.ts and the rhythm overlay/blog presentation): when document.fonts reports the brand fonts ready (or a font loads), clear Pretext measurement caches and re-run layout; make it deterministic (no race), with tests, and verify against the P4-01 baseline (/Users/home/Projects/.baselines/threat-intelligence-20261007/) at 390/768/1280 px: heights equal on every load.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Fixed in Papyrus#155 (squash-merged to develop). Root cause: useBrandFontsReadyVersion only bumped a version number and never called Pretext clearCache(), so per-font widths measured with fallback metrics were reused after the brand fonts loaded. Fix: lib/brand-fonts-watch.ts clears the Pretext cache and then triggers re-layout on initial load and on every loadingdone event (SSR-safe no-op without document.fonts); newspaper.tsx font refresh also clears. Test: test:brand-fonts-watch (in test:ci:ts); brand render snapshots and rhythm layout pass; CI green. NOT yet verified against the 17328/17648 px baseline heights at 390/768/1280 (needs a TI build on the next published Papyrus release), so leaving open.

right_now_summary: Papyrus now clears font width caches and reruns layout when brand fonts load; baseline verification remains.
